description: NASA Mission Intelligence System Evaluation Dataset

questions.question: What was the main objective of Apollo 11?
questions.ground_truth: The main objective of Apollo 11 was to perform a crewed lunar landing and return safely to Earth, accomplishing the national goal set by President Kennedy.

questions.question: Who were the crew members of Apollo 11?
questions.ground_truth: The crew of Apollo 11 consisted of Commander Neil Armstrong, Command Module Pilot Michael Collins, and Lunar Module Pilot Edwin 'Buzz' Aldrin.

questions.question: What malfunction created the emergency in Apollo 13?
questions.ground_truth: An oxygen tank explosion in the Service Module caused the emergency on Apollo 13, leading to loss of electrical power and oxygen supply.

questions.question: What sequence of events followed the Apollo 13 oxygen tank failure?
questions.ground_truth: After the oxygen tank explosion, the crew shut down the Command Module, moved to the Lunar Module as a lifeboat, and executed a free-return trajectory around the Moon to return to Earth.

questions.question: Who were the crew members of Apollo 13?
questions.ground_truth: The crew of Apollo 13 consisted of Commander James Lovell, Command Module Pilot John Swigert, and Lunar Module Pilot Fred Haise.

questions.question: What happened during the Challenger disaster?
questions.ground_truth: The Space Shuttle Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after launch on January 28, 1986, due to the failure of an O-ring seal in the right solid rocket booster, resulting in the loss of all seven crew members.

questions.question: What technical components failed in the Challenger accident?
questions.ground_truth: The primary technical failure was the O-ring seals in the right solid rocket booster's field joint, which failed due to cold temperatures on launch day.

questions.question: What were the key milestones during the Apollo 11 lunar landing?
questions.ground_truth: Key milestones included lunar orbit insertion, Eagle separation, powered descent, landing at Tranquility Base, EVA, sample collection, ascent, docking, and trans-Earth injection.

questions.question: What was the flight plan structure for Apollo 11?
questions.ground_truth: The Apollo 11 flight plan included launch, Earth orbit checkout, trans-lunar injection, lunar orbit insertion, lunar landing, surface operations, lunar ascent, docking, trans-Earth injection, and splashdown.

questions.question: How did the Apollo 13 crew survive the emergency?
questions.ground_truth: The crew survived by using the Lunar Module as a lifeboat, conserving power, managing limited resources, and working with Mission Control to improvise solutions including a CO2 scrubber.

questions.question: What were the communication challenges during Apollo missions?
questions.ground_truth: Communications during Apollo missions were handled through the Manned Space Flight Network with ground stations around the world, maintaining contact except during lunar far-side passes.

questions.question: What was the role of the Command Module Pilot during Apollo 11?
questions.ground_truth: Michael Collins, as Command Module Pilot, remained in lunar orbit aboard Columbia while Armstrong and Aldrin descended to the Moon, conducting observations and preparing for the crew's return.

questions.question: What scientific experiments were conducted during Apollo 11?
questions.ground_truth: Apollo 11 deployed the Early Apollo Scientific Experiments Package, collected lunar samples, and set up a laser ranging retroreflector and passive seismometer.

questions.question: What lessons were learned from the Challenger disaster?
questions.ground_truth: Key lessons included the importance of engineering concerns over schedule pressure, improved communication between NASA and contractors, and redesign of the solid rocket boosters.

questions.question: What was the duration of the Apollo 11 mission?
questions.ground_truth: Apollo 11 lasted approximately 8 days, from launch on July 16, 1969, to splashdown on July 24, 1969, with about 21.5 hours spent on the lunar surface.
